items.to: China Stocks Add $620 Billion as Beijing Pledges Fresh Market Support: What’s Driving the Rally?
sum: China’s stock market staged a powerful rally on November 27 after Beijing signalled stronger measures to support equities, triggering broad buying across mainland exchanges. The gains added an estimated ¥4.1 trillion ($620 billion) in market value, reflecting a sharp improvement in investor appetite following the government’s latest policy message.

Technology and growth-oriented stocks led the advance, with the Shenzhen and ChiNext indexes recording particularly strong gains. The rally has renewed attention on China’s efforts to stabilise its capital markets, but investors are now assessing whether the policy signal can translate into a sustained recovery.

The immediate catalyst was Beijing’s renewed commitment to providing stronger support for the country’s stock market. The announcement raised expectations that financial institutions backed by the state could play a more active role in stabilising equities and improving market confidence.

The prospect of additional support encouraged investors to return to mainland stocks, driving gains across major benchmarks. The Shenzhen Component climbed 7.24%, outperforming the Shanghai Composite, which advanced 3.73%. The ChiNext Index, which tracks growth-oriented companies listed in Shenzhen, surged 11.61%. The broader market also participated in the rally. The STAR 50 Index gained 5.00%, while the CSI 300 advanced 4.17%.

The estimated ¥4.1 trillion increase in market capitalisation highlights the scale of the buying response. However, the gains reflect a market repricing following the policy announcement rather than evidence that underlying economic challenges have already been resolved.
Technology and growth-oriented stocks were among the strongest performers as investors moved back into sectors that had faced pressure from broader market uncertainty.

The ChiNext Index’s 11.61% advance highlights the strength of buying in growth-focused companies. Semiconductor, artificial intelligence, cloud computing and technology-related shares attracted attention as the broader rally improved expectations for China’s domestic technology sector.

sum: SYDNEY: Asian shares eked out a rare rally on Thursday after Wall Street fought back from deep lows, though concerns over the circular financing of AI and a new round of US tariffs made for a muted mood in a holiday-thinned session.
Tech giant Nvidia was again at the centre of the unease after S&P put its credit rating on watch for a possible downgrade citing weaknesses in the chipmaker's management and board oversight.
Nvidia stock ended down 3.9% at $149.30 on Wednesday, $2.3 trillion short of its October peak of $243.37.
Wall Street did recoup most of its initial losses overnight as money moved into other, more defensive, sectors. S&P 500 futures added 0.5% early on Thursday, while Nasdaq futures firmed 0.4%.
Japan's Nikkei gained 1.6% and South Korea's main index rose 1.9%. Japan is down 8% for the month, while South Korea has shed 16% and Taiwan 15%.
Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan edged up 0.6%, but were still off 9% for November so far.
Bond investors are wondering if the broad losses in stocks coupled with doubts on the durability of AI-driven business investment might temper the hawkishness of central banks.

sum: SINGAPORE: Asian stocks tumbled early on Wednesday as fresh US tariff threats hit sentiment and a tech-led rally fizzled, with the region's chip-heavy markets bearing the brunt of the selloff.
MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan was down 2.3%, led by a drop of as much as 5.3% in South Korean shares and a 5.1% decline at the worst point in Taiwan.
Japan's Nikkei 225 fell as much as 2.9%, while S&P 500 e-mini futures were 0.3% lower.
Risk appetite weakened after media reports the Trump administration was preparing to release findings of a trade investigation that could pave the way for new tariff measures.

The US Trade Representative's office is preparing to release the findings of the probe into alleged excess industrial capacity among 16 major US trading partners, including China and the EU, three people with knowledge of the matter told Reuters on Tuesday.

"The re-emergence of tariffs from the USTR has been met with a collective sigh from investors," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone Group Ltd in Melbourne. "Much like the US debt ceiling, which is also making an unwelcome comeback onto the radar, traders appear reluctant to commit significant capital on the headlines alone."

Overnight, stocks on Wall Street were mixed, with the S&P 500 down 0.5% and the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite off 1.5%, while the small-cap Russell 2000 gained 0.6% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average rallied 0.9%. Attention now turns to US core PCE data due on Wednesday ahead of the Thanksgiving holiday later in the week.

items.t: Акции США могут упасть, поскольку ралли Nvidia сходит на нет
sum: US stocks were set to tumble on Tuesday as the early euphoria after Jensen Huang’s return to Nvidia faded, with investors cautious about further AI-driven gains and US inflation data.
Nvidia’s shares dropped nearly 5 percent in US premarket trading, having soared 31.5 percent on Monday after the ‌AI chip giant reinstated Huang as CEO under pressure from US President Donald Trump.

Nasdaq futures fell 2.2 percent after the tech-heavy index climbed by nearly 7 percent the previous day. Anthropic briefly fell below its IPO price of $83, a striking drop only days after the Claude developer’s record-breaking market debut.
The pan-European STOXX 600 index dropped 0.6 percent, weighed down by a sharp slump in miners.

Huang's comeback capped a whirlwind week of events that whipped markets and tore through the AI ecosystem, which has relied on Nvidia for everything from supplying chips to bankrolling the industry’s massive buildout. But it also left unanswered questions over Huang, who had resigned after revelations of extramarital affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy.

“With Jensen’s return, it assures people massively and gives hope that the data centre construction continues and that boosts US GDP,” said Chris Beauchamp, chief market analyst at IG Group in London.

“But it then opens up a whole list of questions that may not be answered very quickly. What did he know? What else did he do? How much went to China? And these questions will continue to chip away at market confidence.”

sum: Taiwan Weighted Index gains more than 3,300 points, regains 40,000 mark
Technology stocks, including TSMC, rise to their price limits
Taiwanese stocks surged 9% on the 24th following news of Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's return. Taiwan is Huang's hometown.

According to Chinese portals Sina.com and Baidu, the Taiwan Weighted Index closed at 40,122.35, up 3,310.46 points (8.99%) from the previous session. The gain was the largest on record. After closing at 36,811.89 the previous day, the index regained the 40,000 mark at the open and climbed as high as 40,180.38 during the session.

TSMC, Taiwan's largest company by market capitalization and a key Nvidia partner, surged to its daily limit-up of 9.85% shortly after the open and held those gains through the close. Major technology stocks also rose to their price limits, including chip designer MediaTek (+9.91%), foundry operator UMC (+9.97%) and Hon Hai Precision Industry (+9.95%).

The Central News Agency reported that 621 stocks hit their daily upper price limits on the day, including those on the over-the-counter market. The surge in Taiwan's stock market is seen as reflecting improved investor sentiment toward artificial intelligence (AI)-related companies after CEO Huang returned to Nvidia's management following his resignation, just 11 days earlier. Earlier, news that Nvidia's board had unanimously decided on Huang's return on the 23rd local time sent the company's shares up 31.48% on the New York Stock Exchange, while TSMC's American depositary receipts (ADRs) gained 14.08%. Japan's benchmark Nikkei 225 Average (Nikkei Index) closed at 58,644, up 2,207 points (3.91%) from the previous session.

items.t: Биржи Китая снизили коэффициент маржи до 80% из-за падения акций
sum: Beijing is handing leveraged traders back the borrowing room it took away ten months ago, while the tech boards it meant to cool sit more than 40% below their peaks. If you hold Chinese stocks, the open question is whether cheaper leverage finds anyone willing to use it.

China's three stock exchanges said on Sunday, November 22, that the minimum margin ratio for buying shares with borrowed money will fall to 80% from 100% on November 30, according to Reuters. The Shanghai, Shenzhen and Beijing bourses have the approval of the China Securities Regulatory Commission, and the change undoes the tightening they ordered in January.
The arithmetic is simple. At 100%, an investor with 1 million yuan of collateral could borrow 1 million yuan. At 80%, the same collateral supports 1.25 million.

The January move, effective January 19, lifted the ratio from 80% to 100% to cool a rally, and it had itself reversed the August 2023 cut from 100% to 80%. So the ratio has now gone 100, 80, 100, 80 in about three years. Frankly, that is a regulator steering by the last few weeks of price action.

The exchanges' own explanation is blunt: "Margin financing activity has weakened significantly recently, while overall leverage is low." Outstanding margin loans have fallen more than 20% to about 2.2 trillion yuan, or $329 billion, from a peak of 3 trillion yuan in late June, Reuters reported. Nobody needs to rein in leverage that has already left.

Yardeni Research says China's STAR 50 index is down 44% from its summer high and property investment fell nearly 22% in October. With AI stocks making up about 42% of China's market value per Goldman Sachs, the firm sees little left to cushion the blow. - Yardeni China AI bubble warning - China AI crash threat to Xi Jinping

The damage is concentrated where the speculation was. BusinessDay reported that the Shanghai Composite fell nearly 3% last week to a 16-month low, while Shanghai's Star Market and Shenzhen's ChiNext have each dropped more than 40% from their June peaks. Those are the boards where chip and software names trade, and where a lot of that borrowed money went in.
items.to: China's exchanges cut the margin ratio to 80% as stocks slide

sum: Chinese AI stocks have collectively lost $1.7 trillion in market value since the end of June, Bloomberg data shows, as reported by indiaipo.in. The sharp fall wipes out the major gains seen in the first half of the year and marks a challenging turn for China’s technology sector.

Indexes that track Chinese tech stocks, including the Hang Seng Tech Index and the onshore ChiNext Index, have now slumped into negative territory for the year. The Hang Seng Tech Index, home to internet giants like Alibaba and Tencent, is at a two-year low.
The ChiNext Index, which hit record highs over the summer, is now down 31% in 2026. The chip-focused Star 50 Index has also fallen back after a record rally.

Much of this reversal comes as global optimism for the AI boom has cooled. According to indiaipo.in, the appeal of Chinese AI as a cheaper alternative to U.S. technology has been shaken by new U.S. moves to further restrict access to advanced chips.
Recent draft rules from Washington have closed loopholes that allowed Chinese companies to rent high-end processors from overseas, making it even harder for Chinese firms to train their AI models.

Bush Chu, investment director for China equities at Aberdeen Investments, told indiaipo.in that investors are now worried about a slowdown in AI capital spending and the long-term viability of U.S.-China supply chain ties. Market volatility has left fund managers “pretty speechless,” as once-hot names like Z. AI Co. and Zhongji Innolight Co. have seen their shares tumble from record highs.

Tencent’s management warned last week that the ongoing crunch in chip supplies could delay its next HY4 AI model, although it hopes the Chinese supply chain can help fill some of the gap. Alibaba has forecast a slowdown in its cloud division’s growth for 2027, but expects a rebound by 2028.

sum: Chinese stock markets took a beating on Friday in a sixth straight day losses, even before a selloff of tech shares on Wall Street accelerated in overnight trading. Around the world, investors are questioning the valuation of tech shares against profit prospects and the massive spending on AI infrastructure.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index declined 1.2 percent on Friday, ending the week with a drop of 2.8 percent. Its tech-focused STAR Market 50 index tanked 3.8 percent this week, with a slump of 11 percent in the STAR Market Composite Index. The Shenzhen Composite Index fell 3.1 percent on Friday, wrapping up the week with a loss of 6.5 percent, and its tech-heavy ChiNext board plunged 8.8 percent in five trading days.
Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index retreated 5.2 percent this week following a drop of 1.9 percent on Friday. Its tech index lost 3.8 percent alone.

"Tech shares continued to be targeted despite repeated expressions of support by Chinese authorities and corporate moves to buy back their shares," said Miao Yanliang, an analyst at the Citic Securities. "Investors are still beset by bearish sentiment, compounded with poor performances of tech shares in overseas markets."

High-profile tech shares led declines. ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT), China's top memory chipmaker, lost 6.2 percent on Friday, while Moore Threads, a designer of graphics processing units, dived 11 percent. Zhongji Innolight, a maker of high-speed optical modules, fell 3.7 percent, and Unitree, China's highest-profile robot maker, slipped 1 percent.

It was the same story in Hong Kong on Friday. Shares in Tencent, a conglomerate with businesses in AI platforms, cloud services and financial technology, fell 1.3 percent after third-quarter revenue missed market forecasts. Z.ai lost 7.2 percent, Minimax plunged 10.8 percent and Kuaishou tanked 11.4 percent. NetEase dived 19 percent after the company reported a decline in third-quarter profit and revenue. Shares of SenseTime, a Chinese AI model and infrastructure firm, were down 3.3 percent even after reporting higher revenue and profit.
There were some bright spots.

sum: Hong Kong's stock market fell sharply on the 20th, led by technology shares, with the Hang Seng Index closing down 1.9% at 22,410.80 from the previous day — its lowest level in about 19 months, since April 30, 2025. On the mainland, the Shanghai Composite Index fell 1.2% and the CSI300 Index dropped 0.8%, both hitting lows not seen since July 2025.

The previous day's U.S. initial public offering by AI developer Anthropic raised $107.3 billion — the largest ever — and its first-day close was 17% above the offering price. But the blockbuster listing failed to restore optimism across AI-related stocks. Some market participants even suggested that selling to free up cash for the IPO contributed to declines in other tech shares.

The Hang Seng Tech Index fell 3.8%. On the mainland, the Shenzhen Composite Index dropped 3.6%, the ChiNext Composite Index for growth companies fell 3.5%, and Shanghai's STAR 50 Index slid 3.1%, with tech-heavy indexes posting the steepest declines.

Among individual stocks, social media giant Tencent (0700.HK) fell 1.3% to HK$344 (approximately $43), sinking to its lowest range since July 2024. Its quarterly results showed AI-related spending squeezing profits and cash flow. Alibaba Group (9988.HK), by contrast, bucked the trend with a 3.5% gain to HK$83.35 (approximately $11), supported by its announcement that adjusted EBITDA for the quarter through September 30 rose 260% year-on-year.

Hong Kong-listed Chinese AI model developers plunged across the board. MiniMax Group fell 10.8% to HK$102.40 (approximately $13), a record low, bringing its weekly decline to more than 30%. Zhipu (Z.ai) also dropped 7.2% to HK$334 (approximately $43), down 18.2% for the week.

Semiconductor shares also weighed heavily on the market, with the related index plunging 3.9%. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSMC) has halted some advanced-chip manufacturing orders from Chinese chip design companies, in principle limiting available technology to older generations, people familiar with the matter said — souring investor sentiment.
This week's market was buffeted by a fresh wave of volatility in AI-related stocks.

Investors have said that Anthropic's market reception over the coming days and weeks will be heavily scrutinized to gauge broader sentiment toward investments in artificial intelligence. The Claude developer's initial public offering was priced at $83 a share, valuing Anthropic at about $1.5 trillion before the stock rose as much as 39% to trade at $115.10.

"Investors are making changes in their portfolio to incorporate Anthropic, so I wouldn't extrapolate a whole lot of meaning from (Thursday's) trading behavior, whether it's up or down," said Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital in St. Louis.
Ellerbroek pointed to a leadership change in chipmaker Nvidia and to shrinking bets on the growth in data center capex as having an impact on investors.
"Data centers are going to be more expensive to build and they're going to be built more slowly," Ellerbroek said.
Anthropic's stock closed up 17% on its debut, valuing the company at just below $1.8 trillion.
"We can't underestimate the importance of this IPO. It sort of serves as a valuation for the wider AI ecosystem," said Fiona Cincotta, senior market analyst at StoneX.

sum: The weakness accompanied commentary on future Federal Reserve financial policy by governor Christopher Waller. Speaking to CNBC, Waller argued the case for hiking interest rates by 50 basis points at the December meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) — more than the current market consensus of 25 basis points.
With CPI inflation above the Fed’s 2% target for five years, he warned that businesses were becoming comfortable passing on 3% annual price rises “or higher” to consumers.
“You might need to, like, shock people to say, ‘Wait a minute; 3% is not the number you should be thinking about going forward,’” he said.

Waller described the need for “aggressive actions” to tackle inflationary trends, which he noted were spreading into areas not directly impacted by current geopolitical catalysts — the US-Iran war and associated spike in oil prices.
The latest data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool showed markets still overwhelmingly favoring a 25-basis-point hike in December, with the odds of that outcome above 95%.
Fed target-rate probabilities by FOMC meeting (screenshot). Source: CME Group

Not everyone shared confidence in the case for policy tightening. Commenting on the Fed’s hawkish posture, economist Robin Brooks argued that the recent cooling in oil prices meant that upping rate-hike commitments was unnecessary.

sum: Bitcoin traded lower on Wednesday despite a rally in the Nasdaq, where Nvidia’s latest earnings results helped ease concerns about the technology sector.

The largest crypto asset was down 1.5% over the past day, trading near $64,000 at press time. Ethereum also declined, falling below $1,800, while Solana and XRP gained approximately 2% each and BNB was unchanged.
The S&P 500 and Nasdaq futures edged higher in early trading, while the VIX fell more than 4.5% from the prior session’s spike.

Nvidia shares rose about 2% after reporting better-than-expected quarterly results and stronger guidance, although uncertainty over its leadership succession, regulatory scrutiny, and tighter US chip-export restrictions kept gains in check.

The market outlook has faced pressure from renewed calls for higher interest rates. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller told CNBC Wednesday that the central bank should consider a 50-basis-point rate increase at its December 8-9 meeting, arguing that inflation was proving more persistent than anticipated.
He said inflation was becoming more widespread, warning that policymakers might need to “shock people” to prevent price growth around 3% from becoming entrenched.

Waller said the central bank should first undo the three quarter-point cuts made in 2025, but indicated that a return to the previous rate level might not adequately address inflation. He said a quarter-point increase in December could be sufficient if the Fed also signals another hike in January. If officials are unwilling to provide that signal, he favors a larger half-point increase immediately.

sum: SINGAPORE: Stocks erased early gains in Asia on Wednesday after Nvidia posted a better-than-expected sales forecast, as investor confidence remained fragile over questions about the company's future leadership and potential impacts on its regional supply chain.

In choppy trade, MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan reversed an initial rally to be down 0.1%, narrowly extending its losing streak into a fifth day. Japan's Nikkei 225 slid 0.3%, while US S&P 500 e-mini futures clung to gains, up 0.3%.

"Nvidia's results were reassuring and gave investors a reason to refocus on earnings, but they haven't resolved the broader questions around AI spending returns, financing sustainability and leadership uncertainty," said Charu Chanana, chief investment strategist at Saxo Bank in Singapore.
"So we are seeing an initial relief rally, but not necessarily the conviction needed for a sustained recovery."

In oil markets, Brent crude futures were 0.6% lower at $92.60 a barrel in Asian trade following data showing an increase in US crude and fuel inventories last week, although the ongoing Middle East conflict and disruptions to shipping through the Strait of Hormuz limited losses.

Nvidia shares slid 0.5% in after-hours trading, having earlier been up as much as 3.8% after the chipmaker, seen as a bellwether for the AI sector, reported both third-quarter revenue and a fourth-quarter forecast that beat market expectations in its first earnings report since Jensen Huang's abrupt departure as CEO this month.

sum: SYDNEY: Asian shares fell on Monday after a whiplash week capped by the shock exit of Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO, with the chipmaker's earnings and Anthropic's IPO this week set to test whether the AI-fuelled bull market still has further to run.

Also later in the week, US President Donald Trump is set to meet Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen to discuss nuclear arms reduction and the US-Israeli war with Iran.

The minutes of the US Federal Reserve's October policy meeting are due on Wednesday, while a parade of Fed speakers will also be on the bill this week. Markets will be alert for any hint of policymakers being receptive to the idea of an outsized 50-basis-point interest rate hike next month.
In Asia on Monday, Japan's Nikkei fell 0.6%, while South Korea slipped 0.2%. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan eased 0.1%.
S&P 500 futures edged up 0.3%, while Nasdaq futures bounced 0.5%.

Nvidia, the poster child of a four-year US bull market, has seen its market value tumble from about $5.8 trillion in early October to $3.9 trillion as of Friday, LSEG data showed, as investors rushed for the exit after Huang's departure.

Analysts expect earnings growth of 90% on revenue of $109 billion in Nvidia's fiscal third quarter when its earnings are due on Tuesday, LSEG data showed, with all eyes on whether the chipmaker will stick to its bullish outlook for next year under new management.

items.t: Акции SanDisk упали более чем на 50% из-за угрозы китайских чипов и высоких прибылей
sum: SanDisk (SNDK) has declined over 53% from its June 2026 peak, trading at $1,096.10 as of July 29. The downturn stems from CXMT’s successful $8.6 billion IPO and reports of Apple testing Chinese DRAM, which threaten the NAND pricing thesis that fueled SanDisk’s rally. As a pure-play NAND firm, SanDisk lacks diversification, intensifying the impact of these supply-side shifts. Investors are focused on the August 5 earnings report, where management must address long-term pricing power and enterprise SSD demand. With an RSI near 22, the stock is deeply oversold, with critical support at $1,000 and $924.90.

TradingKey - SanDisk (NASDAQ: SNDK) is trading at $1,096.10 on Wednesday July 29, down from Monday's close of $1,278.23, with today's range $1,050.72 to $1,188.00. Shares are now more than 53% off the all-time high of $2,354.39 reached on June 25, 2026, after a 52-week run from $40.10 that briefly made SNDK one of the most extraordinary performers in the market.

The collapse began with CXMT's blockbuster Shanghai IPO on July 27, which surged 466% on debut following an $8.6 billion raise Asia's largest semiconductor IPO of 2026 reigniting fears that Chinese NAND supply could erode the pricing environment that drove SanDisk's rally. August 5 earnings are the next hard catalyst. Average analyst target: $2,217.77.

SanDisk's bull case through the first half of 2026 rested on a single structural argument: AI-driven enterprise SSD demand was growing faster than global NAND supply, keeping prices elevated and margins wide. That argument worked while CXMT was a Chinese domestic curiosity with limited international scale. The $8.6 billion IPO that surged 466% on its Shanghai STAR Market debut changed the market's assessment of how seriously to take Chinese NAND competition.

A company that can raise $8.6 billion in a single IPO has the capital to build substantial manufacturing capacity over a two to four year horizon. Even if CXMT cannot compete with SanDisk on enterprise SSD technology today, the supply side signal is what the market is repricing.
The Apple testing report added a demand-side dimension.

items.t: Китайские фондовые рынки не могут полностью избавиться от медвежьих настроений
sum: Chinese stock markets remained on edge this week, with investor sentiment tilting bearish and tech shares remaining under pressure as the shock from the resignation of high-profile Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang reverberated through global markets.

The benchmark Shanghai Composite Index fell 0.6 percent on Friday and 0.4 percent for the week. Its Nasdaq-style STAR Market 50 index tumbled 2.3 percent on Friday but managed a 1.8 percent gain for the week. The Shenzhen Component Index lost 1.9 percent for the week, and the tech-heavy ChiNext board retreated 1.3 percent after tanking 3.3 percent on Friday. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell 1.6 percent on Friday for a weekly loss of 3.5 percent. Its tech index dropped 3 percent.

The sharp decline in tech stocks was, in part, due to Huang's departure from the AI tech giant he co-founded and ran for three decades. He quit after revelations of an extramarital affair. In China's tech realm, Victory Giant Technology and TFC Communications dropped by the daily limit of 10 percent on Friday. Shares in optical transceiver giant Zhongji Innolight tumbled 8.4 percent, Eoptolink lost 8.8 percent, and electronics maker Foxconn retreated 7.5 percent.

"The exit of Jensen Huang from Nvidia is due to have a huge impact, but at the moment, it's unclear how huge," said Dai Qing, an analyst with Changjiang Securities. "Suppliers and customers of Nvidia in China will have to wait for an evaluation, as well as will the rest of the world."

A Morgan Stanley gauge of Chinese mainland investor sentiment from November 5-11 fell 16 percentage points to 15 percent, with trading volumes contracting. The bank said it remains cautious on Chinese stocks, but favors shares traded on the Chinese mainland over those traded in Hong Kong.

Overall, Chinese equities have lost about US$3.5 trillion in value since May. To bolster the market, Beijing has taken steps to facilitate more equity investment by state-backed funds and more company share buybacks. The China Securities Regulatory Commission reiterated at an investor conference in Shanghai on Thursday that "there is long-term certainty in China's development, which lays a solid foundation for investment."

items.t: На фондовом рынке Китая в конце сессии наблюдался всплеск объемов защитных покупок; Фондовые ETF поглотили почти 600 миллиардов юаней за два месяца
sum: Акции технологических компаний упали во время сессии 13 ноября в материковом Китае, но объем торгов в нескольких ETF (биржевых фондах) с широкой базой данных внезапно вырос во второй половине дня, при этом на заключительной сессии появился плотный оборот - сигнал, который рынок интерпретировал как вступление капитала в поглощение продаж. Статистика показывает, что с 28 сентября по 12 ноября совокупный чистый приток ETF акций составил 593,826 млрд юаней (приблизительно 89,0 млрд долларов США), хотя за последние три торговых дня потоки превратились в чистый отток.

Во второй половине дня 13 ноября торги ETF на широкой основе явно накалились. Tianhong CSI 300 ETF торговался на 738 млн юаней (приблизительно 110,7 млн ​​долларов США) за весь день, установив рекорд с момента листинга ETF, при этом активность была сосредоточена на заключительной сессии. За сессию ETF GF CSI 300 торговал на сумму 336 миллионов юаней (приблизительно 50,4 миллиона долларов США), из которых 279 миллионов юаней (приблизительно 41,8 миллиона долларов США) перешли из рук в руки за последние 25 минут, то есть более 80% объема было сконцентрировано до закрытия.

В отраслевых ETF также наблюдался всплеск объемов в конце сессии. Объем торгов ETF Huabao Securities за последние 35 минут составил более 800 миллионов юаней (приблизительно 120,0 миллионов долларов США), а оборот за полный день составил 1,274 миллиарда юаней (приблизительно 191,0 миллиона долларов США); За последние 20 минут объем торгов ETF GF Media составил более 300 миллионов юаней (приблизительно 45,0 миллионов долларов США), а оборот за полный день составил 891 миллион юаней (приблизительно 133,6 миллиона долларов США). Что касается более крупных флагманских продуктов, оборот E Fund ChiNext ETF и ChinaAMC STAR 50 ETF каждый превысил 11 миллиардов юаней (приблизительно 1,6 миллиарда долларов США) за однодневный оборот, в то время как ETF ChinaAMC STAR Semiconductor также достиг 10 миллиардов юаней (приблизительно 1,5 миллиарда долларов США).

Глядя на потоки средств, можно сказать, что эта волна покупок ETF наблюдается уже некоторое время. С 28 сентября ETF акций фиксировали чистый приток в течение 26 торговых дней подряд, а затем с 10 по 12 ноября начался чистый отток, причем только 12 ноября чистый отток составил 25,434 миллиарда юаней (приблизительно 3,8 миллиарда долларов США). За период с 28 сентября по 12 ноября совокупный чистый приток достиг 593,826 млрд юаней (приблизительно 89,0 млрд долларов США).

items.t: Акции США растут, поскольку CoreWeave ослабляет опасения по поводу расходов на ИИ
sum: NEW YORK: US stocks closed higher on Wednesday, with the S&P 500 and the Nasdaq each rallying more than 1% as earnings from neocloud firm CoreWeave cooled investor concerns about the durability of the AI trade, while Nvidia stabilized after two straight sessions of sharp declines.
Battered CoreWeave shares surged 24.7%, their biggest daily percentage jump in more than three months, to close at the highest level in two weeks.

The company said it would become profitable in the first half of 2028 on an adjusted basis, seeking to reassure investors that strong demand and customer commitments could support its debt-fueled expansion.
Sentiment improvedacross AI infrastructure stocks, as Nebius Group surged 15.4% and Applied Digital shot up 7.4%.

Nvidia advanced after shedding about US$430 billion of market capitalisation in the previous two sessions as investors worried about CEO Jensen Huang's relationship with a businesswoman alleged to be a Chinese spy.

Equities have been volatile in recent days. Investors have expressed concerns about more regulation in the AI space after sweeping Democratic victories in the US midterm elections last week. That, and worries about Nvidia's leadership, pressured one of the biggest pillars of the current bull market.
Contributing to choppy stock trading, investors have been encouraged by cooling oil prices but concerned by hot inflation data that pushed Treasury yields sharply higher.

sum: NEW YORK/LONDON: Major stock indexes rallied on Monday as Brent crude oil fell more than 5% after US President Donald Trump said he is unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran, while shares of Nvidia dropped.
The fall in oil prices helped to ease worries about inflation that have weighed on economies across the globe this year.

Trump on Sunday said that he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the war progressed, even though both countries reported that shipping had been hit in or near the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude futures fell $5.75, or 5.85%, to settle at $92.57 a barrel, and prices continued falling after settlement, while US West Texas Intermediate futures dropped $3.98, or 4.38%, to $86.85.
Efforts to end the Iran war have gathered pace following last week's US midterm elections in which Democrats won control of Congress.

Shares of Nvidia, the second-most valuable company in the world, tumbled 4.2% and closed at their lowest level since April 7, with investors questioning CEO Jensen Huang's future at the AI chipmaker after an internal investigation into whether a foreign intelligence effort had targeted him.

However, the three major US stock indexes finished more than 2% higher, with the S&P 500 rebounding from its biggest weekly drop since April 2025. Last week's selloff was tied to the US midterm elections and worries about increased AI and data center regulation.

"We have seen a very steep and exaggerated selloff in the market," said Adam Sarhan, chief executive of 50 Park Investments in New York. "Whenever the market gets that stretched to the downside, history has shown us usually it's a good buying opportunity in the short term."

items.t: Спад в сфере искусственного интеллекта возрождает игнорируемые рынки Азии
sum: BEIJING: The unravelling of the artificial intelligence (AI) trade after the US midterm elections is forcing investors to rethink their Asia playbook, reviving demand for out-of-favour Chinese and Indian stocks as well as companies poised to benefit from easing inflation and trade tensions.
Aberdeen Investments favours markets powered by stronger domestic growth, including India and Vietnam, and sees upside in Chinese technology firms.
Hedge fund Lotus Asset Management is long Hong Kong equity futures, while Allianz Global Investors is looking at healthcare and consumer companies.
Asia has been among the hardest hit by the market fallout from the Democrats’ sweep of Congress.

Many of the region’s biggest stocks – from Samsung Electronics Co and SK Hynix Inc to Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co – are critical suppliers to the global AI build-out, leaving local markets especially exposed as investors brace for greater scrutiny of the industry and question whether massive spending on computing infrastructure will generate sufficient returns.
“I expect investors to diversify more broadly and reduce their concentration in the AI trade,” said Rajeev De Mello, global macro portfolio manager at Gama Asset Management SA.
“This should be supportive of China and other markets where valuations are less demanding. India could also benefit, although its dependence on imported energy remains a headwind,” he added.

sum: In this week’s wrapup, we discuss China’s AI bubble, Binance’s $6 billion crypto heist, India’s booming astrotech industry, the challenges of expanding the country’s strategic petroleum reserves, and the Indian beer industry through the lens of Carlsberg’s UDRHP.
Also, here’s a quick note before we dive in. We’ll be taking a publishing holiday tomorrow, November 8th, for Diwali. We’ll be back with a new story on November 9th. Have a safe and happy Diwali!

In just four months, the STAR 50, China’s main index of AI stocks, has fallen about 40%. That wiped out nearly $480 billion of investor wealth. Over the same period, the Nasdaq in the US barely moved.

Part of the reason lies in how the rally started. Beijing wanted to depend less on US tech, so state-backed funds poured money into chipmakers, robotics firms and AI labs. Retail investors saw that backing as a signal to buy.
So is this only China’s problem, or an early warning for AI stocks everywhere? Read the full story here.
Binance, the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, was hacked last week, with hackers stealing over $6 billion worth of crypto in just 20 minutes.

And Binance is far from alone. Bybit lost roughly $1.5 billion in 2025, WazirX lost over $230 million in 2024, and more than $1.31 billion was lost across 344 incidents in just the first half of 2026.

sum: SINGAPORE: US stock futures slid and the dollar softened on Wednesday as investors girded for results from US midterm election with the focus on whether Democrats can wrest control of Congress from President Donald Trump's Republicans.
Democrat Jon Ossoff won re-election in Georgia, marking the first significant race call of the night as polls closed in seven states.
Democrats are favoured to capture the House and both parties are locked in an intense state-by-state battle for the Senate, leaving investors and markets on edge.

"For traders, the distinction between a narrow Democratic majority and a commanding victory is critical," said Chris Weston, head of research at Pepperstone. "A narrow blue wave may be largely priced in."

In the US Senate, where at least nine races are seen as competitive, Democrats won the first of 35 seats up for grabs on Tuesday, with US Senator Mark Warner winning reelection in Virginia as expected. Democrats need to net four seats to win control of that chamber.
Weston said the greatest market reaction may come not from who wins Congress, but from how decisively they win and how far the result deviates from expectations.
Futures for S&P 500 slid 0.5% while Nasdaq futures fell 0.9%.
items.to: US stock futures dip as investors await midterm election results

sum: KUALA LUMPUR: BURSA Malaysia opened higher on Tuesday, buoyed by gains in banking stocks despite a mixed overnight performance on Wall Street and continued selling pressure on technology and semiconductor counters.
Overnight, the S&P 500 declined 0.51% to 7,541.40 points. The Nasdaq dropped 1.07% to 25,164.32 points, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average rose 0.41% to 51,983.98 points.
The FBM KLCI rose 3.03 points, or 0.19%, to 1,622.54 at 9.19am, after opening 1.25 points higher at 1,620.76, supported by gains in banking stocks.
Banking stocks led the gains, with Hong Leong Bank rising 20 sen to RM21.38, RHB Bank adding 18 sen to RM7.68, AmBank climbing 14 sen to RM6.41 and Maybank gaining six sen to RM10.04.
Other gainers included Nestlé, which surged 42 sen to RM96.54, and United Plantations, which rose four sen to RM29.34.

In contrast, technology and semiconductor stocks dominated the losers' list, led by Malaysian Pacific Industries, which tumbled 58 sen to RM39.20. ViTrox shed 30 sen to RM10.18, Mi Technovation fell 27 sen to RM6.03 and UWC lost 17 sen to RM6.92.

sum: MANILA (Reuters): Emerging Asian currencies edged lower against the dollar on Monday, while equities were mixed as investors digested the AI rout and awaited a raft of inflation data.

An MSCI gauge of emerging-market currencies slipped 0.2% against a steady dollar as markets looked ahead to US midterm elections that could determine control of Congress and shape spending priorities. The Singapore dollar lost 0.2% and the Taiwan dollar shed 0.6%.

The South Korean won weakened to 1,346.90 per US dollar, its lowest since mid-October. Analysts at MUFG said the won continues to be underpinned by favourable macroeconomic conditions, though persistent foreign selling of equities has diluted support for the currency.
South Korean shares rose 2.2%, with dip-buying in technology stocks helping the market look past the AI-driven selloff on Wall Street on Friday after weak results from Intel and Amazon.
Data showed South Korean exports nearly doubled in October, marking their sharpest increase in more than five decades, as strong global demand for AI investment boosted chip shipments.
Singapore's benchmark stock index slid 1.4%, weighed down by banking stocks ahead of earnings from DBS and OCBC, bringing losses from its early-September record high to nearly 10%.
In Indonesia, stocks fell as much as 1.5% before reversing course to trade up 0.9%, with investors awaiting inflation and third-quarter economic growth data due later this week.

sum: Stocks to buy | Shares to buy | Ganesh Dongre's stock recommendations: The Indian equity benchmarks ended the week on a positive note, with the Nifty gaining nearly 2% to close at 23,053, while the Bank Nifty advanced 0.75% to settle at 54,686. However, the Nifty 50 index witnessed buying interest at lower levels and recovered towards the 23,200 mark, although it continues to face resistance at higher levels. Sectoral performance remained broadly positive, with most major sectors witnessing gains in the range of 2%–7%.

The Pharma sector emerged as the top performer, rallying nearly 7% during the week. However, despite the recovery in domestic equities, Brent crude oil remains elevated, hovering in the $110–$115 per barrel range, keeping inflationary concerns and global uncertainties in focus.

Ganesh Dongre, AVP — Equity Research at Anand Rathi, believes a sustained weekly close of the Nifty 50 index above 23,200–23,400 would improve the near-term technical outlook of the Indian stock market. Ganesh Dongre of Anand Rathi said that both the Nifty 50 and Bank Nifty index remain in a cautious technical phase. The rebound from oversold levels has improved near-term sentiment; however, a sustained recovery will require the Nifty to establish itself above the 23,200–23,400 resistance zone and subsequently reclaim the 24,000–24,200 range. Similarly, the Bank Nifty needs to move decisively above 56,400–56,500 to strengthen its technical outlook.

“Until these crucial resistance levels are convincingly breached, markets are likely to remain volatile, with intermittent recovery attempts, range-bound consolidation and selling pressure at higher levels. Traders should therefore maintain a cautious approach and closely monitor key support and resistance levels, along with Brent crude oil prices and geopolitical developments, for confirmation of the next directional move,” Ganesh Dongre of Anand Rathi said.

Speaking on the Nifty 50 outlook for next week, the Anand Rathi expert said the 50-stock index witnessed a notable rebound from the 22,500–22,200 support zone and recovered towards the 23,200 level by the end of the week. This support area remains crucial, as it represents a significant historical support zone near previous yearly and quarterly lows.
